issues.legal_issue: Disputes concerning leases governed by general property law are arbitrable when the tenancy is not governed by a special statute that provides statutory protection against eviction and an exclusive forum.
material_facts: The dispute arose from a sub-lease containing an arbitration clause.
The premises and tenancy were not governed by a special rent statute and were governed by general property law.
The parties had agreed to arbitrate disputes arising out of or in connection with the sub-lease.
issues.conclusion: The dispute was arbitrable, and there was no impediment to invoking the arbitration clause.
issues.legal_principle: Under the principle in Booz Allen and Hamilton Inc. v. SBI Home Finance Ltd., disputes are generally arbitrable unless expressly or by necessary implication reserved for public fora. Natraj Studios (P) Ltd. v. Navrang Studios and Booz Allen concern tenancies governed by special statutes, not ordinary leases governed by the Transfer of Property Act, 1882. Vidya Drolia v. Durga Trading Corporation clarified that such ordinary lease disputes are arbitrable and overruled the contrary observations in Himangni Enterprises v. Kamaljeet Singh Ahluwalia. Where a special rent statute applies, its statutory tenant protections and exclusive forum make the dispute non-arbitrable.

rule.if: tenancy_arbitrability_proceeding and lease_governed_by_general_property_law and not special_statutory_tenant_protection_applies and arbitration_agreement_exists

predicates.tenancy_arbitrability_proceeding: A proceeding concerns whether a dispute arising from a landlord-tenant relationship may be resolved by arbitration.
predicates.lease_governed_by_general_property_law: The lease and tenancy are governed by general property law rather than a special rent statute.
predicates.special_statutory_tenant_protection_appl: A special statute provides the tenant statutory protection against eviction and assigns adjudication to a specified court or forum.
predicates.arbitration_agreement_exists: The landlord and tenant agreed to arbitrate disputes arising from their lease.

issues.definition: When a tenancy arbitrability proceeding concerns a lease governed by general property law, no special statutory tenant protection applies, and the parties agreed to arbitrate, the tenancy dispute is arbitrable.

issues.legal_issue: An arbitrator deciding an arbitrable lease dispute may consider statutory relief against forfeiture when the relevant conditions arise in the arbitration.
material_facts: The sub-lease was governed by general property law and contained an arbitration clause.
The Court considered the statutory provisions concerning determination of leases and relief against forfeiture for non-payment of rent or certain other breaches.
The Court held that a tenant could raise the relevant circumstances before the arbitrator in proceedings seeking ejectment.
issues.conclusion: An arbitrator may consider the statutory relief against forfeiture and make an appropriate award when the relevant circumstances arise in an arbitration concerning a lease governed by general property law.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 111, 114 and 114A of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 address determination of leases and relief against forfeiture. The protections under Sections 114 and 114A do not make such disputes non-arbitrable: they provide equitable relief, including discretionary relief under Section 114. Namdeo Lokman Lodhi v. Narmadabai supports the principle that relief under Section 114 is discretionary and is not invariably required to be granted in favour of the tenant.

rule.if: lease_tenancy_arbitration_proceeding and ejectment_claim_based_on_forfeiture and (rent_arrears_tendered or remediable_breach_cured)

predicates.lease_tenancy_arbitration_proceeding: An arbitrator is resolving a dispute arising from a lease or tenancy governed by general property law.
predicates.ejectment_claim_based_on_forfeiture: The landlord seeks ejectment on the basis that the lease was determined by forfeiture.
predicates.rent_arrears_tendered: The tenant pays or tenders rent in arrears in the proceeding.
predicates.remediable_breach_cured: The tenant remedies a breach that is capable of remedy.

issues.definition: In a lease-tenancy arbitration involving an ejectment claim based on forfeiture, if the tenant tenders arrears or cures a remediable breach, the arbitrator may consider relief against forfeiture.

issues.legal_issue: The Supreme Court, rather than a different court named in the arbitration agreement, has authority to appoint an arbitrator in an international commercial arbitration appointment proceeding.
material_facts: The petitioner was an individual who was a national of Kenya and habitually resident in Kenya.
The dispute arose under an arbitration agreement with an Indian company.
The arbitration clause stated that the Delhi High Court would appoint the sole arbitrator if the parties disagreed about the appointment.
The petitioner sought appointment of an arbitrator by the Supreme Court.
issues.conclusion: Because the arbitration qualified as an international commercial arbitration, the Supreme Court was to appoint the arbitrator under Section 11(6) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, notwithstanding the contractual reference to appointment by the High Court.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2(1)(f) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 includes an arbitration in which at least one party is an individual who is a national of, or habitually resident in, a country other than India. For an international commercial arbitration appointment, Section 11(6) assigns appointment authority to the Supreme Court; a contractual provision naming a High Court does not displace that statutory authority.

predicates.international_commercial_arbitration_app: A proceeding seeks the appointment of an arbitrator for an arbitration that qualifies as international commercial arbitration.
predicates.individual_party_is_foreign_national_or_: At least one party is an individual who is a national of, or habitually resident in, a country other than India.
predicates.arbitration_agreement_exists: The parties agreed to submit their dispute to arbitration.

issues.definition: When an appointment proceeding concerns an international commercial arbitration involving an individual who is a foreign national or habitually resident abroad, the Supreme Court has authority to appoint.

issues.legal_issue: A court may appoint the arbitrator nominated by a party where the arbitration agreement provides for a sole arbitrator and the other party does not respond or object to the nomination.
material_facts: The arbitration clause provided for a sole arbitrator to be mutually agreed by the parties and for appointment through a court if they disagreed.
The petitioner invoked the arbitration clause, proposed a sole arbitrator, and sought the respondent's concurrence.
The respondent did not reply to the appointment notice and did not appear to oppose the appointment petition.
issues.conclusion: The Court allowed the petition and appointed the sole arbitrator proposed by the petitioner.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 11(6) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, the Court may make the appointment where the agreed appointment process has not resulted in an appointment. In this case, the sole-arbitrator clause, the proposed nomination, and the respondent's failure to respond or object supported appointment of the proposed arbitrator.

rule.if: arbitrator_appointment_proceeding and sole_arbitrator_clause_exists and party_proposed_sole_arbitrator and other_party_did_not_respond_or_object

predicates.arbitrator_appointment_proceeding: A proceeding seeks court appointment of an arbitrator under an arbitration agreement.
predicates.sole_arbitrator_clause_exists: The parties agreed that their dispute would be decided by a sole arbitrator.
predicates.party_proposed_sole_arbitrator: A party invoked the arbitration agreement and proposed a person to serve as sole arbitrator.
predicates.other_party_did_not_respond_or_object: The other party neither responded to the appointment request nor objected to the proposed arbitrator.

issues.definition: In an arbitrator appointment proceeding, if the parties agreed to a sole arbitrator, one party proposed a person, and the other party neither responded nor objected, the court appoints the proposed sole arbitrator.
